acceptance_cases.counterexample: An inner occurrence claim stores a settlement, command, occurrence, or batch root and makes the canonical dependency recursive.
acceptance_cases.given: The exact local occurrence claim is nested inside the complete OwnedSettlementV2 commitment.
acceptance_cases.invariant: No value inside the settlement depends on a root or identifier derived after the settlement.
nonclaims: Acyclicity alone does not authenticate or semantically validate the settlement.
acceptance_cases.then: Every downstream field and backward dependency edge rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Settlement and command identities remain acyclic
acceptance_cases.when: The inner field registry and complete dependency graph are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A B1A-valid configuration is rebound to a historical state and then described as store-current.
acceptance_cases.given: Configuration validity, exact-state binding, and datastore currentness are separate facts.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The binder proves configuration authority for one exact state candidate; only atomic publication establishes store currentness.
nonclaims: The state binder and publication shell are not implemented by this revision.
acceptance_cases.then: Root, deployment, and activation mismatches reject, while historical state remains candidate evidence only.
acceptance_cases.title: Exact-state binding does not overclaim currentness
acceptance_cases.when: The binding laws, exact predecessors, and currentness policy are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: The alleged fresh replay receives the submitted provisional fee claim tuple through the whole settlement.
acceptance_cases.given: OwnedSettlementV2 contains both claim-independent settlement material and submitted local fee claims.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Replay receives one exact non-authoritative projection whose closed fields exclude every submitted local fee claim.
nonclaims: The replay projection is a design value without an independent canonical root.
acceptance_cases.then: Any projection field that carries the submitted claim tuple rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Replay input is claim-erased by construction
acceptance_cases.when: The projection field and forbidden-field registries are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A replay helper reads the claim-bearing settlement, command, or admitted claim tuple directly.
acceptance_cases.given: Fresh replay depends on the projection, intents, exact state, state-bound configuration, and authenticated context.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The recomputed tuple has exactly five claim-erased and independently sourced predecessors.
nonclaims: The exact V2 replay implementation remains a later checkpoint.
acceptance_cases.then: Every whole-settlement, whole-command, submitted-claim, missing-source, or extra-source edge rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Replay predecessor closure is exact
acceptance_cases.when: The graph predecessor set and forbidden replay edges are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Changing only a submitted fee amount changes the tuple described as independently recomputed.
acceptance_cases.given: Two settlements have equal replay projections and all independent replay sources are equal.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Claim-only mutation preserves the replay projection and recomputed tuple, causing admitted-versus-recomputed equality to reject the mutation.
nonclaims: This design law is not yet an executable information-flow proof.
acceptance_cases.then: Every contract that permits submitted claims to influence recomputation rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Claim-only mutations satisfy replay noninterference
acceptance_cases.when: The complete noninterference law set is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A malicious submitted claim tuple is accepted without equality against fresh replay.
acceptance_cases.given: Admission owns one submitted tuple and claim-erased replay derives one expected tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Exact equality of admitted and recomputed tuples is the only constructor of the exact controlled claim tuple.
nonclaims: The controlled tuple is an unimplemented design value.
acceptance_cases.then: Deleting either equality predecessor or adding a third loose tuple rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: One controlled claim tuple closes replay equality
acceptance_cases.when: The equality node and its two source edges are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Claims and occurrence identifiers are stored as separately alignable parallel tuples.
acceptance_cases.given: Occurrence identity depends on one controlled claim and the complete command root.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Each controlled occurrence owns exactly one exact claim and its derived occurrence identifier.
nonclaims: The paired controlled-occurrence carrier is not implemented here.
acceptance_cases.then: An independent occurrence-ID tuple or caller-supplied identifier field rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Claim and command-bound identity form one owned pair
acceptance_cases.when: The controlled-occurrence and batch field registries are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Two correct occurrence identifiers are swapped across claims at settlement ordinals 1 and 3.
acceptance_cases.given: The controlled claim tuple has a fixed strict settlement-ordinal order.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Pair count, pointwise claim equality, command-root derivation, ordering, and identifier uniqueness are all exact.
nonclaims: The exact occurrence-ID byte preimage remains a later codec checkpoint.
acceptance_cases.then: Swap, truncation, extension, duplication, foreign ordinal, and tuple-index derivation mutants reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Controlled occurrence pairing is pointwise
acceptance_cases.when: Every occurrence pairing law and exact predecessor is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: The batch stores both paired occurrences and a separately supplied occurrence-ID tuple.
acceptance_cases.given: Claims and identifiers are read-only projections of the one paired tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The future witness batch owns one exact controlled-occurrence tuple and no parallel claim or ID tuple.
nonclaims: The witness-batch root preimage is not frozen by this revision.
acceptance_cases.then: Every duplicate tuple, root, version, or language field rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: The batch uses one minimal paired occurrence aggregate
acceptance_cases.when: The controlled and forbidden batch-field registries are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A V2 normalizer consumes only claim amounts and drops command-bound occurrence identities.
acceptance_cases.given: The controlled batch owns the exact paired occurrence tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The V2 occurrence normal form consumes only the batch-owned paired tuple and commits every ordered occurrence identifier in lineage.
nonclaims: The current V1 contiguous-position SLNF adapter remains nonconforming for this V2 surface.
acceptance_cases.then: Claim-only, loose-pair, copied-ID, re-enumerating, and identity-dropping consumer paths reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Downstream lineage consumes the paired batch value
acceptance_cases.when: The downstream source and normal-form predecessor set are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A positive-fee fill after a zero-fee fill is renumbered from settlement ordinal 1 to tuple index 0.
acceptance_cases.given: Positive-fee claims retain their original positions in the complete settlement fill tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Settlement fill ordinals are bounded, strictly increasing, potentially sparse, and are the only ordinal source for occurrence identity.
nonclaims: The concrete V2 cardinality validator is not implemented.
acceptance_cases.then: Re-enumeration, duplicate, out-of-range, zero-fee, missing-positive, and reordered claims reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Sparse original fill identity remains exact
acceptance_cases.when: The exact claim cardinality policy is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A future batch accepts independently swappable roots and policy versions beside nested exact sources.
acceptance_cases.given: Every repeated fact is derivable and revalidatable from one nested exact source.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The batch constructor contains only seven nested exact sources, ending in one paired occurrence tuple.
nonclaims: Derived properties still require point-of-use validation in a later implementation.
acceptance_cases.then: Every independently swappable duplicate field rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Controlled batch construction remains minimal
acceptance_cases.when: The batch field registry and exact graph fan-in are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A failed composite operation returns a state-bound configuration, controlled pair, normal form, or downstream authority-like value.
acceptance_cases.given: Admission, state binding, replay, equality, pairing, normalization, and later publication are ordered phases.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Composite rejection exports no intermediate controlled value or successor-producing authority.
nonclaims: Independent inputs may remain internally available to their original owner.
acceptance_cases.then: Removing any phase-specific forbidden output from the closed registry rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Composite rejection is authority-empty
acceptance_cases.when: The exact no-authority-output registry is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A design repair is treated as permission to implement a witness batch or mount value-moving authority.
acceptance_cases.given: Carrier bytes, replay code, pairing, normalization, publication, and migration remain unimplemented or excluded.
nonclaims: No runtime or authority-bearing implementation is approved.
acceptance_cases.then: Implementation and mount authority remain false and all nonclaims remain explicit.
acceptance_cases.title: Design evidence cannot promote runtime authority
acceptance_cases.when: The phase flags, nonclaim registry, and exact target diff are checked.

nonclaims: Revision 3 implements no OwnedSettlementV2 carrier or canonical codec.
The claim-erased replay projection and noninterference relation are not implemented.
The state-bound configuration, paired occurrences, and witness batch are not implemented.
The current V1 SLNF adapter is not a conforming V2 paired-occurrence consumer.
An exact-state binder does not prove datastore currentness.
The exact V2 command schema and root preimage are not frozen.
No state, configuration, transition, receipt, bundle, proof, publication, datastore, or mount authority exists.
Python and Rust parity is not established.

source_roles.authenticated_command_bytes: freshly reauthenticated bytes used for extraction and command identity only
source_roles.downstream_occurrence_consumption: only the exact paired tuple nested in the controlled witness batch
source_roles.exact_pre_state_v2: exact candidate state; store currentness exists only inside later publication
source_roles.exact_settlement_replay_projection_v2: non-authoritative claim-erased view with no independent root
source_roles.state_bound_active_configuration_v2: fresh binder output for the same exact state candidate used by replay
source_roles.submitted_claims: equality targets only and never replay inputs
source_roles.validated_active_configuration_claim_v2: B1A-valid content with no state authority before binding
